core.Health/max: A hundred hit points: a round number every damage figure is read against (CMB-01)

core.Resistance/pierce: No armour: every unit is unarmoured until its template says otherwise
core.Resistance/crush: No armour: every unit is unarmoured until its template says otherwise
core.Attack/Melee/hack: No melee attack: a unit whose amounts are all 0 has none (CMB-02)
core.Attack/Melee/pierce: No melee attack: a unit whose amounts are all 0 has none (CMB-02)
core.Attack/Melee/crush: No melee attack: a unit whose amounts are all 0 has none (CMB-02)
core.Attack/Melee/reach: A block between the two bodies' edges, an arm's length
core.Attack/Melee/prepare: Half a second's wind-up before the first blow, so an attack reads
core.Attack/Ranged/hack: Zero by default: a unit has no ranged weapon until its template supplies damage and range (M5, CMB-04)
core.Attack/Ranged/pierce: Zero by default: piercing damage belongs to an explicitly configured ranged weapon (M5, CMB-04)
core.Attack/Ranged/crush: Zero by default: blunt ranged damage requires an explicit weapon (M5, CMB-04)
core.Attack/Ranged/fire: Zero by default: incendiary ranged damage requires an explicit weapon (M5, CMB-04)
core.Attack/Ranged/range: Zero blocks disables ranged attacks on existing units (M5, CMB-04)
core.Attack/Ranged/prepare: Sixteen ticks to draw a bow before its first shot, the M5 starting archer wind-up
core.Attack/Ranged/repeat: Twenty-five ticks between shots, the M5 starting archer rhythm
core.Attack/Ranged/speed: Four blocks per tick: a twenty-block arrow flight takes five ticks (M5 implementation finding 8)
core.Attack/Ranged/spread: A horizontal Gaussian standard deviation of 2.25 blocks at 100 blocks, scaled linearly with distance (M5, CMB-04; implementation finding 8)
core.Attack/Ranged/highGround/rangePerBlock: 5 % more range a block above the target: 0 A.D.'s reach by height (M5, CMB-16)
core.Attack/Ranged/highGround/damagePerBlock: 4 % more damage a block above the target: AoE II's damage from above (M5, CMB-16)

core.Behaviour/flee: Units stand their ground unless their template says they run
core.Behaviour/stance: Aggressive, 1: a unit fights what it sees unless its template says otherwise (M5, CMB-05, 0 A.D.'s default)

strategos:template/unit_base.UnitMotion/walkSpeed: 3.75 blocks a second, a little under a walking player's 4.3, so a crowd reads as marching; M1's movement baselines are measured at it (D-11)
strategos:template/unit_base.UnitMotion/turnRate: Degrees a tick: a full turn in eight ticks, quick enough for orders to feel immediate, slow enough to see the turn
strategos:template/unit_base.Body/width: A player's hit box, so the vanilla humanoid model fits (D-04)
strategos:template/unit_base.Body/height: A player's hit box, so the vanilla humanoid model fits (D-04)
strategos:template/unit_base.Body/radius: The avoidance radius, a little over half the width, so a dense crowd still shows gaps between bodies (M1, PATH-06)

strategos:unit/debug_walker.UnitMotion/walkSpeed: Five blocks a second: the movement tests' brisk walker, never a game unit

strategos:template/unit_infantry.Look/weapon: Zero: the starting equipment tier of the weapon, raised to one by iron weapons (TECH-03); a tier, not a stat, so it carries no balance of its own
strategos:template/unit_infantry.Look/armour: Zero: the starting equipment tier of the armour, raised to one by chainmail (TECH-03); a tier, not a stat, so it carries no balance of its own

strategos:unit/infantry.Loot/resources/food: Eleven food: 0 A.D.'s infantry loot of five food plus a tenth of its cost's sixty (research mechanics 1.21); winning a fight pays, so a raid on soldiers refunds a fraction, never the price (CMB-13)
strategos:unit/infantry.Loot/resources/wood: Four wood: a tenth of its forty wood cost, 0 A.D.'s share of cost (research mechanics 1.21); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16 (CMB-13)
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Melee/hack: With 100 hit points and resistance 5, one spearman kills another in 29 blows, about half a minute at a blow a second (M2, CMB-02)
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Melee/reach: A spear reaches a little past an arm's length
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Melee/prepare: Half a second's wind-up before the first thrust, so a charge reads
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Melee/bonus/Cavalry: 2.5 times the damage against cavalry: a braced spear stops a charge, so spearmen beat horsemen at equal cost (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/infantry.Resistance/hack: 0.9^5 lets 59 % through: shield and padding make a fight between two spearmen last tens of seconds
strategos:unit/infantry.Resistance/crush: Padding does little against blunt blows; crush belongs to cavalry and siege later
strategos:unit/infantry.Cost/resources/wood: Forty wood: the shaft and the shield; wood gathered early goes to both houses and soldiers
strategos:unit/infantry.Cost/population: One house's room for one soldier, as for a worker
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Structure/fire: Six fire a blow: ten spearmen burn a wooden house in 7 s and a stone civic centre in about a minute and a quarter. Measured in M6 T23 (QA-12): a squad of four at three fire needed 1.7 to 4.4 minutes for a barracks, storehouse or arsenal and 5.9 for a civic centre, longer than the 8 to 12 minutes the winner has left after a centre falls, so matches did not end; doubled so a squad of four burns a wooden building in about a minute. A raid still hurts and takes several minutes to end a base (CMB-03, D-12); our own value, tuned against QA-12
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Structure/prepare: Half a second to light the torch and reach the wall, as the spear's wind-up
strategos:unit/infantry.Attack/Structure/repeat: A blow of fire a second, the spear's rhythm
strategos:unit/infantry.Capture/strength: Two and a half a second, 0 A.D.'s infantry: the unit that captures (CMB-10)
strategos:unit/infantry.Promotion/value: A hundred: food 60 plus wood 40, what it costs to replace: the sum of its resource cost, so a kill is worth the price of the fallen and a veteran army is the wealth of what it has beaten; our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16 (CMB-11)

strategos:unit/archer.Loot/resources/food: Eleven food: five food plus a tenth of its sixty, as the spearman's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/archer.Loot/resources/wood: Four wood: a tenth of its forty (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/archer.Loot/resources/iron: Two iron: a tenth of its twenty (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/archer.Health/max: Seventy hit points, tuned up from fifty (duel matrix, M5 UNIT-07): archers must outlast the spearmen's approach and a hill duel must run long enough for height to tell, yet stay under a spearman's hundred
strategos:unit/archer.UnitMotion/walkSpeed: 0.2 blocks a tick: slightly faster than infantry, allowing ranged positioning (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Attack/Ranged/pierce: Sixteen pierce per arrow, tuned up from six (duel matrix, M5 UNIT-07): a spearman's resistance 5 lets only 59 % through, and archers of equal cost must break the spearmen before and after contact
strategos:unit/archer.Attack/Ranged/range: Twenty blocks: the archer can engage well before melee contact (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Attack/Ranged/prepare: Sixteen ticks to draw the first shot, making the wind-up readable (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Attack/Ranged/repeat: Twenty ticks between arrows, tuned down from twenty-five (duel matrix, M5 UNIT-07): a volley a second, the spearman's own rhythm
strategos:unit/archer.Attack/Ranged/speed: Four blocks per tick: the starting projectile speed for analytic lead (M5 CMB-04)
strategos:unit/archer.Attack/Ranged/spread: 2.25 blocks at 100 blocks: starting Gaussian spread for analytic shots (M5 CMB-04)
strategos:unit/archer.Vision/range: Thirty-two blocks: enough to acquire targets beyond the twenty-block firing range (M5 CMB-04)
strategos:unit/archer.Resistance/hack: One armour: light protection makes close combat dangerous (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Resistance/pierce: One armour: the archer has light protection from arrows (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Resistance/crush: One armour: the archer has light protection from blunt blows (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Cost/resources/food: Sixty food: the same provision as a worker or spearman (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Cost/resources/wood: Forty wood: the bow and its ammunition, as much wood as a spearman (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Cost/resources/iron: Twenty iron: arrowheads add an iron cost to ranged troops (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/archer.Cost/population: One house's room for one archer, as for other infantry
strategos:unit/archer.Capture/strength: Two and a half, as 0 A.D.'s ranged infantry (CMB-10)
strategos:unit/archer.Promotion/value: A hundred and twenty: food 60, wood 40 and iron 20, what it costs to replace: the sum of its resource cost, so a kill is worth the price of the fallen and a veteran army is the wealth of what it has beaten; our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16 (CMB-11)

strategos:unit/horseman.Loot/resources/food: Thirteen food: five food plus a tenth of its eighty (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/horseman.Loot/resources/wood: Four wood: a tenth of its forty (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/horseman.Loot/resources/iron: Three iron: a tenth of its thirty (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/horseman.Look/weapon: Zero: the starting equipment tier of the weapon, raised to one by iron weapons (TECH-03); a tier, not a stat, so it carries no balance of its own
strategos:unit/horseman.Look/armour: Zero: the starting equipment tier of the armour, raised to one by chainmail (TECH-03); a tier, not a stat, so it carries no balance of its own
strategos:unit/horseman.Health/max: Two hundred hit points, tuned up from a hundred and twenty (duel matrix, M5 UNIT-07): twice a spearman, the price of being hard to catch, enough to live through the archers' fire to the melee
strategos:unit/horseman.UnitMotion/walkSpeed: 0.34 blocks a tick: nearly twice the spearman, so cavalry can run archers down (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/horseman.Attack/Melee/hack: Ten hack per sword stroke, tuned up from five (duel matrix on the real terrain, M5 UNIT-07): over three times a spearman's three, so the counter over archers is quick
strategos:unit/horseman.Attack/Melee/reach: A block and a half: a sword from the saddle reaches a little past a spear's thrust
strategos:unit/horseman.Attack/Melee/prepare: Eight ticks of wind-up: a rider strikes while still at the gallop
strategos:unit/horseman.Attack/Melee/repeat: A stroke every eighteen ticks, a little faster than the spearman's thrust a second
strategos:unit/horseman.Resistance/hack: Three armour: a shield and a padded jerkin, lighter than the spearman's five (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/horseman.Resistance/pierce: Two armour: spears are meant to counter cavalry, so pierce gets through (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/horseman.Resistance/crush: Two armour: padding does little against blunt blows, as for the spearman
strategos:unit/horseman.Cost/resources/food: Eighty food: a rider and a horse eat more than a foot soldier (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/horseman.Cost/resources/wood: Forty wood: the shield and the saddle, as much as a spearman's shaft and shield
strategos:unit/horseman.Cost/resources/iron: Thirty iron: a sword and horseshoes, the dearest of the three soldiers in iron (M5 UNIT-07)
strategos:unit/horseman.Cost/population: One house's room for one rider, as for a foot soldier; the horse needs none (UNIT-06)
strategos:unit/horseman.Body/width: A horse's hit box, 1.4 blocks, the mounted body's size (ADR-0011, UNIT-06)
strategos:unit/horseman.Body/height: Two blocks: a horse and the rider above its saddle (ADR-0011, UNIT-06)
strategos:unit/horseman.Body/radius: The large class's avoidance radius, 0.7: half the body's width (PATH-11)
strategos:unit/horseman.Capture/strength: One and three quarters, 0 A.D.'s cavalry: raiders burn rather than take (CMB-10)
strategos:unit/horseman.Abilities/charge/cooldown: Six hundred ticks, thirty seconds: a charge is once a skirmish, not a stance, and the rest outlasts the burst six times over; our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16 (UNIT-10)
strategos:unit/horseman.Abilities/charge/effects: Its three numbers, from spec 2.7's showcase, each our own starting value to be tuned against QA-16 (UNIT-10): five seconds (a hundred ticks), about a charge's length across a skirmish map at the boosted pace and short enough to be a decision; walk speed times one and a half, so the horseman crosses archers' range in two thirds of the time; hack times one and a fifth, a ten becomes a twelve per stroke, the lance's momentum
strategos:unit/horseman.Promotion/value: A hundred and fifty: food 80, wood 40 and iron 30, what it costs to replace: the sum of its resource cost, so a kill is worth the price of the fallen and a veteran army is the wealth of what it has beaten; our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16 (CMB-11)

strategos:unit/ram.Loot/resources/wood: Thirty wood: a fifth of its hundred and fifty, double a soldier's share, since siege is the costly prize of a fight (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/ram.Loot/resources/iron: Fourteen iron: a fifth of its seventy, double a soldier's share (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/ram.Health/max: Five hundred hit points: ten times a worker, two and a half horsemen; a ram is slow, so it has to outlast the arrows on the way to the wall (CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.UnitMotion/walkSpeed: A tenth of a block a tick: half a spearman's pace, so a ram is seen coming and a force must escort it (CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Attack/Melee/crush: Forty crush a swing of the log: against a stone building two rams raze a civic centre in under a minute, where the same price in torch-bearers takes about three (over five before M6 T23 doubled the torch) (D-12, CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Attack/Melee/reach: A block and a half, a log's swing from the front of the frame
strategos:unit/ram.Attack/Melee/prepare: Twenty ticks: the log is drawn back before it swings
strategos:unit/ram.Attack/Melee/repeat: A swing every forty ticks, two seconds: heavy and slow, twenty crush a second a ram
strategos:unit/ram.Resistance/hack: One armour: a roof of planks, so soldiers beat a ram in melee, which is its counter (CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Resistance/pierce: Eight armour: arrows glance off the roof, as the classics' siege shrugs off archers; 0.9^8 lets 43 % through (CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Resistance/crush: Three armour: a ram hurts a ram less than it hurts a house
strategos:unit/ram.Cost/resources/wood: A hundred and fifty wood: the frame, the roof and the wheels (CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Cost/resources/iron: Seventy iron: the log's cap; two rams cost 440 resources, which buys only four spearmen, so a ram still beats torches on stone, three minutes for four spearmen (row 14 said five before M6 T23 doubled the torch) (D-12, CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Cost/population: Three: a ram is a team of men, so two rams are a spearman squad's room and a siege is felt in the housing
strategos:unit/ram.Body/width: Two blocks: the frame and its wheels, the `unit_large` type's size (ADR-0011, CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Body/height: Two blocks: the roof's ridge over the wheels (ADR-0011, CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Body/radius: One block, half the width: the large class's avoidance radius, so a ram keeps others off its frame (PATH-11, CMB-09)
strategos:unit/ram.Promotion/value: Two hundred and twenty: wood 150 and iron 70, what it costs to replace: the sum of its resource cost, so a kill is worth the price of the fallen and a veteran army is the wealth of what it has beaten; our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16 (CMB-11)

strategos:unit/worker.Loot/resources/food: Three food: a twentieth of its sixty, a small prize, half a soldier's share, since workers fight no one and a raid on them already costs their owner the work (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/worker.Health/max: Half a spearman's: a raid on workers costs their owner dearly, so workers are worth guarding
strategos:unit/worker.Behaviour/flee: Eight blocks from a blow: out of a spearman's reach, near enough to go back to work
strategos:unit/worker.Behaviour/stance: Passive: a worker never fights; hit, it runs from the blow (M5, CMB-05)
strategos:unit/worker.Cost/resources/food: Sixty food: the civic centre's first worker pays back its cost in about a minute of berry picking
strategos:unit/worker.Cost/population: One house's room for one worker
strategos:unit/worker.Cost/time: Ten seconds: a civic centre with a full queue adds a worker every ten seconds, the pace the first house's timing target (1:30) assumes
strategos:unit/worker.Builder/rate: One builder's worth: a building's time is what one worker takes, and more builders add with diminishing returns (BLD-03)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/food/fruit: A berry a second: a bush's sixty food in a minute, so the first worker pays back its own cost quickly
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/food/grain: Half a berry picker's: a field's farmers are its steady food, five of them about two a second together (ECO-09)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/wood/tree: Slower than picking: a log's twenty wood in about half a minute, so an oak keeps a worker busy for a few minutes
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/stone/rock: Slower than chopping: a block's five stone in about twelve seconds, so a rock outcrop is a lasting job and stone stays dearer than wood (ECO-07)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/capacities/food: Ten food a trip: short trips, so a bush near the centre keeps food coming steadily
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/capacities/wood: Ten wood a trip, half a log: eight trips pay for the first house (the timing target, 1:30)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/capacities/stone: Ten stone a trip, two blocks: twenty trips pay a civic centre's two hundred
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/iron/ore: A little slower than stone: a mine's iron is the scarcest resource, so iron sets the pace of an army (ECO-08)
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/capacities/iron: Ten iron a trip, as stone
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/rates/food/meat: As fruit's: a carcass is the quickest food once killed, which pays for the walk to the herd
strategos:unit/worker.ResourceGatherer/slaughter: Hit points a blow, one a second: a sheep in four, a chicken in two
strategos:unit/worker.Capture/strength: One a second, 0 A.D.'s civilian: workers can take an empty house, slowly (CMB-10)
strategos:unit/worker.Promotion/value: Sixty: its food cost, what it costs to replace: the sum of its resource cost, so a kill is worth the price of the fallen and a veteran army is the wealth of what it has beaten; our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16 (CMB-11)

resource_yield.#minecraft:logs: Twenty wood a log: an oak of four or five logs holds about ninety, a few minutes of one worker's chopping
resource_yield.#minecraft:leaves: Leaves yield nothing: they are the canopy that thins as a tree is felled (ECO-03)
resource_yield.#minecraft:base_stone_overworld: Five stone a block of rock: indexed now, gathered from ECO-07 (M4)
resource_yield.#c:ores/iron: Ten iron a block of ore: indexed now, gathered from ECO-08 (M4)
resource_yield.minecraft:wheat: A field's crop: its food is the field's own amount, not the block's (ECO-09)
resource_yield.minecraft:sweet_berry_bush: Sixty food a bush, a worker's cost; a bush left alone fills again in ten minutes, but an emptied one stays empty: early food that runs out, so fields matter (ECO-09)

strategos:building/civic_centre.Loot/resources/wood: Sixty wood: 0 A.D.'s civic centre pays sixty wood (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Loot/resources/stone: Sixty stone: 0 A.D.'s civic centre pays sixty stone (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Loot/resources/iron: Fifty iron: 0 A.D.'s civic centre pays fifty metal, our iron (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Attack/Building/arrows: Three arrows a volley: a lone raider is punished, a raid of four is hurt but not stopped; garrisoned units add more (CMB-07, BLD-11)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Attack/Building/perGarrisoned: One more arrow for each unit inside, so sheltering workers makes the centre deadlier (BLD-11, from T10)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Attack/Building/interval: Eighty ticks (four seconds) between volleys: slow enough that soldiers, not the centre, decide a fight (CMB-07)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Attack/Building/pierce: Eight pierce an arrow, half an archer's sixteen: the centre is a deterrent for early raids, not a tower (CMB-07)
strategos:building/civic_centre.GarrisonHolder/capacity: Twenty inside, workers and foot soldiers only (Worker and Infantry; horsemen stay out): every worker of an early town fits, and the arrows they add (one each) are the centre's answer to a raid (BLD-16, BLD-11)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Attack/Building/range: Twenty-four blocks, four more than an archer: the centre covers its fields and its workers' walk (CMB-07)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Health/max: Two thousand: ten spearmen with torches take minutes, so a raid alone does not end a match (CMB-03)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Cost/resources/wood: Three hundred wood: a second centre is a late, deliberate expansion, not an opening move
strategos:building/civic_centre.Cost/resources/stone: Two hundred stone: stone matters from M4; until then only the starting centre exists
strategos:building/civic_centre.Cost/time: Two and a half minutes: the largest build of the first loop
strategos:building/civic_centre.Housing/capacity: Twenty: the five starting workers and fifteen more before the first house is needed
strategos:building/civic_centre.Placement/spacing: Sixty-four blocks between centres: a second centre claims new ground, not a corner of the first's
strategos:building/civic_centre.Cost/resources/iron: A hundred iron: a second centre's tools and fittings, a late investment (ECO-08)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Limit/count: One civic centre a faction until phases (Town) allow more, as in the classics (BLD-08)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Trainer/batchExponent: Five in 5^0.8 ≈ 3.6 units' time: a batch saves 28 %, worth tying the money up for (PROD-02, as the classics)
strategos:building/civic_centre.TerritoryInfluence/weight: The highest weight: nothing outweighs a civic centre (TERR-01)
strategos:building/civic_centre.TerritoryInfluence/radius: A root of 56 blocks: 0 A.D.'s 140 m at the ×0.4 of M9's scale (spec §1.6 row 6); the highest weight, so a centre's land is its own (TERR-01)
strategos:building/civic_centre.TerritoryInfluence/root: A root: land flood-connected to a centre is connected (TERR-01)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Placement/territory: Own or neutral land, 0 A.D.'s rule: a new centre claims ground nobody holds, never an enemy's (TERR-02)
strategos:building/civic_centre.GarrisonHolder/heal: One hit point a second for each unit inside: 0 A.D.'s civic centre heals garrisoned units 1 HP/s (research second-pass 1.13), so a wounded squad recovers in the town while it holds (BLD-10)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Capturable/points: Two thousand points, its own health: 0 A.D.'s centre holds 2,500 against 3,000 health, ours keeps the ratio near one (CMB-10, M9 spec §2.6)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Capturable/regen: Thirty a second, 0 A.D.'s R28 centre: twenty infantry (50 a second) take an empty centre in 100 s (CMB-10)
strategos:building/civic_centre.Capturable/garrisonRegen: Each unit inside adds its own capture strength to the regeneration, 0 A.D.'s rate of 1 (BLD-10)

strategos:template/building_base.Resistance/fire: Stone: 0.9^7 lets 48 % of a torch's fire through, so wood burns more than twice as fast per hit point (CMB-03)
strategos:template/building_base.Health/max: Five hundred: what a structure without its own figure holds; a deposit has it too, though nothing in M4 attacks one
strategos:template/building_base.DamageStages/first: The first blocks fall once a seventh of the building is gone, early enough to show an attack is working (BLD-05, 04 §11.8)
strategos:template/building_base.DamageStages/second: Two thirds of its hit points left: a third of its blocks down, the building plainly hurt
strategos:template/building_base.DamageStages/third: A third left: most of it down but its walls' foot, a ruin still standing until its last hit points
strategos:template/building_base.Placement/territory: Own territory only, 0 A.D.'s rule: a town grows inside its borders (TERR-02, replacing BLD-02's 48-block stand-in)
strategos:template/building_base.GarrisonHolder/ejectBelow: A tenth of its health: 0 A.D.'s garrison holders let everyone out below 10 % (research second-pass 1.13), so a falling building does not bury its garrison (BLD-10)

strategos:building/house.Loot/resources/wood: 16 wood: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/house.Health/max: Four hundred: a house burns in well under a minute to a squad (CMB-03)
strategos:building/house.Cost/resources/wood: Eighty wood: a worker's first trip or two to a tree; the first house by 1:30 (the timing target)
strategos:building/house.Housing/capacity: Five: a house a few trainings, so housing paces growth
strategos:building/house.Resistance/fire: Timber and thatch: fire's whole blow lands, twice as fast per hit point as stone (CMB-03)
strategos:building/house.TerritoryInfluence/weight: A building's weight: below a centre's, above a quarry's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/house.TerritoryInfluence/radius: Sixteen blocks: 0 A.D.'s 16–20 m houses at ×0.4, rounded up so a house still claims its own tiles beside a road (TERR-01)
strategos:building/house.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)

strategos:building/house.Capturable/garrisonRegen: Each unit inside adds its own capture strength to the regeneration, 0 A.D.'s rate of 1 (BLD-10)

strategos:building/field.Health/max: Two hundred: a field burns quickly, a cheap thing to raid
strategos:building/field.Cost/resources/wood: Sixty wood: a worker's first two trips to a tree, after the berries run low
strategos:building/field.Cost/time: Twenty seconds: a field goes in faster than a house
strategos:building/field.Footprint/obstructs: No: farmers stand on their field, and units walk through the crop
strategos:building/field.Field/amount: Three hundred food a sowing: five farmers reap it in about two and a half minutes
strategos:building/field.Field/ripenTime: Thirty seconds to ripen, while its farmers wait
strategos:building/field.Field/reseed/wood: Forty wood to sow again: cheaper than a new field, so a reseed is the habit (D-14)
strategos:building/field.Resistance/fire: Timber and thatch: fire's whole blow lands, twice as fast per hit point as stone (CMB-03)

strategos:building/barracks.Loot/resources/wood: 40 wood: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/barracks.Loot/resources/stone: 20 stone: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/barracks.Loot/resources/iron: 10 iron: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/barracks.Health/max: Twelve hundred: between a house and the centre
strategos:building/barracks.Cost/resources/wood: Two hundred wood: the barracks by 4:00 (the timing target) after a house and steady chopping
strategos:building/barracks.Cost/resources/stone: A hundred stone: soldiers need the quarry, so stone matters from the first barracks; the first loop's starts bring a hundred (ECO-07, BLD-08)
strategos:building/barracks.Resistance/fire: Timber and thatch: fire's whole blow lands, twice as fast per hit point as stone (CMB-03)
strategos:building/barracks.Cost/resources/iron: Fifty iron: the spear points and helmets of the barracks' armoury; the first loop's starts bring a hundred (ECO-08)
strategos:building/barracks.Trainer/batchExponent: As the civic centre's: one rule for every trainer until a technology changes it (TECH-05)
strategos:building/barracks.TerritoryInfluence/weight: A building's weight: below a centre's, above a quarry's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/barracks.TerritoryInfluence/radius: Twenty-four blocks: a military building claims more than a house, three tiles each way (TERR-01)
strategos:building/barracks.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/barracks.Capturable/points: Eight hundred: a military building is worth holding, more than a house (CMB-10; 0 A.D.'s default 500 at our larger health)
strategos:building/barracks.Capturable/regen: Ten a second, 0 A.D.'s barracks and towers (CMB-10)
strategos:building/barracks.Capturable/garrisonRegen: Each unit inside adds its own capture strength to the regeneration, 0 A.D.'s rate of 1 (BLD-10)

strategos:building/tower.Loot/resources/wood: 20 wood: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/tower.Loot/resources/stone: 30 stone: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/tower.Attack/Building/arrows: One arrow a shot: a tower is a single bowman on a wall, so it wears a raid down but never stops one (BLD-17, CMB-07)
strategos:building/tower.Attack/Building/interval: Forty ticks (two seconds) between arrows: half the centre's pause, a steady five pierce a second that two or three towers turn into a real wall of arrows (BLD-17)
strategos:building/tower.Attack/Building/pierce: Ten pierce an arrow, more than the centre's eight and under an archer's sixteen: a tower hurts a spearman but is no match for a squad (BLD-17)
strategos:building/tower.Attack/Building/range: Twenty-eight blocks, four beyond the centre and eight beyond an archer: it covers the ground an archer would have to cross to answer it (BLD-17)
strategos:building/tower.Vision/range: Twenty-four: it sees about as far as it shoots, a little under an archer's thirty-two, so a tower on a ridge is a lookout too (BLD-17)
strategos:building/tower.Health/max: A thousand: half the centre's, as much as a barracks and a bit less; ten torch-bearers take half a minute to tear it down (CMB-03)
strategos:building/tower.Cost/resources/wood: A hundred wood: the beams and the platform, cheap enough to place several (BLD-17)
strategos:building/tower.Cost/resources/stone: A hundred and fifty stone: stone is the tower's price, so a boom player's quarry buys defence (P4, BLD-17)
strategos:building/tower.Cost/time: A minute and a quarter for one builder: slower than a barracks, so a tower is raised before the raid, not during it
strategos:building/tower.TerritoryInfluence/weight: A building's weight: below a centre's, above a quarry's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/tower.TerritoryInfluence/radius: Twenty-four blocks: as the barracks; a tower holds its chokepoint's land (TERR-01)
strategos:building/tower.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/tower.GarrisonHolder/capacity: Five infantry: 0 A.D.'s towers hold three to five infantry (research second-pass 1.13), the top of that range for a Town building, infantry only (BLD-10)
strategos:building/tower.Attack/Building/perGarrisoned: One more arrow for each unit inside: 0 A.D.'s towers add an arrow per garrisoned infantry (research second-pass 1.13), so a full tower fires six (BLD-11)
strategos:building/tower.Capturable/garrisonRegen: Each unit inside adds its own capture strength to the regeneration, 0 A.D.'s rate of 1 (BLD-10)

strategos:building/sentry_tower.Loot/resources/wood: 20 wood: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Attack/Building/arrows: One arrow a shot and one more for each of its three garrisoned infantry: a sentry post is a lookout with a bow, so it warns and wears a raid down but, empty, is no defence (BLD-12, BLD-11)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Attack/Building/perGarrisoned: One more arrow for each unit inside, as the defence tower's: 0 A.D.'s sentry tower adds an arrow per garrisoned infantry too (research second-pass 1.6), so a full one fires four (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Attack/Building/interval: Forty ticks (two seconds) between arrows, the defence tower's pace: the two differ in reach, health and garrison, not in rhythm (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Attack/Building/pierce: Eight pierce an arrow, the centre's and under the defence tower's ten: wood and a lighter bow hit softer than stone (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Attack/Building/range: Twenty-four blocks, four under the defence tower's: it covers a chokepoint but not the ground beyond it (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Vision/range: Twenty: a lookout sees well past a house but four blocks short of the defence tower (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Health/max: Four hundred: 0 A.D.'s sentry tower holds 400 against the defence tower's 1,000 (research second-pass 1.6); a house's, so a squad with torches takes it down in well under a minute (BLD-12, CMB-03)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Resistance/fire: Timber: fire's whole blow lands, as on a house (CMB-03)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Cost/resources/wood: A hundred wood: 0 A.D.'s sentry tower costs 100 wood (research second-pass 1.6); wood alone, so it is a Village building a lone woodcutter's camp can afford (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Cost/time: Forty seconds for one builder: just over half the defence tower's seventy-five, a post to be raised on the way to a ford (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.TerritoryInfluence/weight: A building's weight: below a centre's, as a house's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.TerritoryInfluence/radius: Twenty blocks: between a house's sixteen and a tower's twenty-four, a lookout holds some of its ground (TERR-01)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.GarrisonHolder/capacity: Three infantry: the low end of 0 A.D.'s three to five for towers (research second-pass 1.13), infantry only (BLD-10, BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Capturable/points: Four hundred: as a house's; it is half the defence tower's points, so the upgrade doubles what a raid must take (CMB-10, BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Capturable/regen: Five a second: as a house's, half a tower's (CMB-10)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Capturable/garrisonRegen: Each unit inside adds its own capture strength to the regeneration, 0 A.D.'s rate of 1 (BLD-10)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Upgrade/time: Fifty seconds: two thirds of the defence tower's build time, since the frame stands and only the stone is fitted; 0 A.D.'s own upgrade takes longer, but a held chokepoint must not stay unmanned for long (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Upgrade/Cost/resources/wood: Fifty wood: 0 A.D.'s tower upgrade costs 50 wood and 100 stone (research second-pass 1.6) (BLD-12)
strategos:building/sentry_tower.Upgrade/Cost/resources/stone: A hundred stone: 0 A.D.'s upgrade price (research second-pass 1.6); with the post's hundred wood and the upgrade's fifty, a defence tower reached through the sentry costs 150 wood and 100 stone, a little more wood than building it outright (BLD-12)

strategos:building/palisade.Loot/resources/wood: 3 wood: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/palisade.Health/max: Three hundred a segment: under a house's four hundred, so a squad with torches or a ram opens a segment in seconds yet a lone raider does not get through (BLD-13, CMB-03)
strategos:building/palisade.Resistance/fire: Timber: fire's whole blow lands, as on a house (CMB-03)
strategos:building/palisade.Cost/resources/wood: Fourteen wood a four-block segment, wood alone: a palisade is a Village structure (research second-pass 1.6), cheap enough that a line of twenty blocks is seventy wood and a starting economy can wall a chokepoint (BLD-13)
strategos:building/palisade.Cost/time: Eight seconds for one builder: a segment goes up faster than a house (30 s) so a line is raised in the minutes before a raid, not after it (BLD-13)
strategos:building/palisade.Wall/segment: Four blocks a segment: a wall's unit of length, whole blocks so a line cuts into end-to-end segments with no gap (BLD-13)

strategos:building/palisade_gate.Loot/resources/wood: 4 wood: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/palisade_gate.Health/max: Five hundred: a little over a segment's three hundred, so a gate is a line's strong point rather than the first thing a raid breaks (BLD-13)
strategos:building/palisade_gate.Resistance/fire: Timber: fire's whole blow lands, as on a house (CMB-03)
strategos:building/palisade_gate.Cost/resources/wood: Twenty wood: a segment's fourteen and a share for the hinges, so a gate costs a little over a segment (BLD-13)
strategos:building/palisade_gate.Cost/time: Ten seconds for one builder: a little over a segment's eight (BLD-13)
strategos:building/palisade_gate.Wall/segment: Four blocks, as a segment: a gate replaces one in a line and fills its place exactly (BLD-13)
strategos:building/palisade_gate.Wall/gate: Marks the segment's middle two columns as a gate: 0 A.D.'s gates open for allies (research second-pass 1.6), so its owner and allies pass and enemies do not (PATH-12, BLD-13)

strategos:building/arsenal.Loot/resources/wood: 40 wood: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/arsenal.Loot/resources/stone: 30 stone: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/arsenal.Health/max: Fifteen hundred: a stone workshop, tougher than a barracks (1,200), so the siege line is not lost to the first raid that reaches it (CMB-09)
strategos:building/arsenal.Cost/resources/wood: Two hundred wood: the frames and the beams a ram is hung from, as a barracks' (CMB-09)
strategos:building/arsenal.Cost/resources/stone: A hundred and fifty stone: the arsenal is a Town building, paid for from the quarry as the tower is (CMB-09, D-12)
strategos:building/arsenal.Cost/time: A minute and a half for one builder: the longest build of the town, so rams come after the army, not before it (CMB-09)
strategos:building/arsenal.Trainer/batchExponent: As the civic centre's: one rule for every trainer until a technology changes it (TECH-05)
strategos:building/arsenal.TerritoryInfluence/weight: A building's weight: below a centre's, above a quarry's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/arsenal.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/arsenal.Capturable/regen: Ten a second: as the barracks (CMB-10)
strategos:building/arsenal.Capturable/garrisonRegen: Each unit inside adds its own capture strength to the regeneration, 0 A.D.'s rate of 1 (BLD-10)

strategos:building/temple.Loot/resources/wood: 20 wood: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/temple.Loot/resources/stone: 40 stone: a fifth of its cost, a building's share above a soldier's tenth and far below the civic centre's (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13); our own starting value, to be tuned against QA-16
strategos:building/temple.Health/max: Twelve hundred: as a barracks, a stone hall: worth a raid but not the first thing a raid breaks, so the army's wounded have somewhere to rest (CMB-12)
strategos:building/temple.Cost/resources/wood: A hundred wood: the roof beams and the benches, half an arsenal's (CMB-12)
strategos:building/temple.Cost/resources/stone: Two hundred stone: the dearest stone bill of the Town buildings, a hall of quartz, so healing is bought from the quarry as the tower and the arsenal are (CMB-12, D-12)
strategos:building/temple.Cost/time: Eighty seconds for one builder: between the tower's seventy-five and the arsenal's ninety, the army's rest is raised after its barracks, not before (CMB-12)
strategos:building/temple.Trainer/batchExponent: As the civic centre's: one rule for every trainer until a technology changes it (TECH-05)
strategos:building/temple.TerritoryInfluence/weight: A building's weight: below a centre's, above a quarry's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/temple.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/temple.Capturable/regen: Ten a second: as the barracks (CMB-10)
strategos:building/temple.Capturable/garrisonRegen: Each unit inside adds its own capture strength to the regeneration, 0 A.D.'s rate of 1 (BLD-10)
strategos:building/temple.GarrisonHolder/capacity: Ten inside, workers, foot soldiers and healers: a temple rests a company, where the civic centre's twenty shelters a town (BLD-10, CMB-12)
strategos:building/temple.GarrisonHolder/heal: Three hit points a second for each unit inside, three times the civic centre's one: 0 A.D.'s temple heals garrisoned units 3 HP/s against the centre's 1 (research mechanics, garrisons), so a wounded squad is whole again in about half a minute, but only by leaving the field (BLD-10, CMB-12)

strategos:unit/healer.Loot/resources/food: Fifteen food: five food plus a tenth of its hundred (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/healer.Loot/resources/iron: Three iron: a tenth of its thirty (research mechanics 1.21, CMB-13)
strategos:unit/healer.Health/max: Sixty: a little above a worker's fifty and well under a spearman's hundred: a healer behind the line is reached only once the line is broken, and then dies quickly (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Behaviour/flee: Eight blocks from a blow, as a worker: a healer runs rather than fights (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Behaviour/stance: Passive: a healer never picks a fight; it heals, and hit, it runs from the blow (CMB-05, CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Attack/Melee/hack: One hack, a third of a spearman's three: a staff to push off a straggler, no threat to a soldier (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Attack/Melee/reach: A block and a fifth, as the spearman's reach (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Attack/Melee/prepare: Ten ticks, as the spearman's wind-up (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Attack/Melee/repeat: A blow a second, as the spearman's rhythm (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Cost/resources/food: A hundred food: 0 A.D.'s healer costs 100 food (research mechanics, healing), dearer than a spearman's sixty, since a healer is worth keeping alive (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Cost/resources/iron: Thirty iron: 0 A.D.'s healer costs 30 metal (research mechanics, healing), as a horseman, so an army's healers are a deliberate buy of the scarcest resource (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Cost/population: One house's room for one healer, as for a foot soldier
strategos:unit/healer.Capture/strength: One a second, as a worker: a healer helps to take an empty house, slowly, and no more (CMB-10, CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Promotion/value: A hundred and thirty: food 100 plus iron 30, what it costs to replace: the sum of its resource cost, so a kill is worth the price of the fallen (CMB-11)
strategos:unit/healer.Abilities/heal/range: Twelve blocks: 0 A.D.'s healer reaches 12 m (research mechanics, healing), short of an archer's twenty, so a healer stands behind its line and reaches most of a squad around it (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Abilities/heal/cooldown: Forty ticks, two seconds: 0 A.D.'s healer heals every 2 s (research mechanics, healing); one healer mends one unit at a time, so a squad needs several (CMB-12)
strategos:unit/healer.Abilities/heal/effects: Five hit points a pulse, two and a half a second: 0 A.D.'s healer restores 5 HP every 2 s (research mechanics, healing), so a healer tops a squad up between fights and does not undo a fight in progress; the temple's garrison heal (3 a second a unit) is the faster cure, which asks the unit to leave the field (CMB-12)

strategos:building/quarry.Deposit/slots: Three workers at a small quarry: a third of a field's, so stone comes slower than food

strategos:building/quarry_large.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)

strategos:building/iron_mine.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)

strategos:building/iron_mine_large.Deposit/slots: Six workers at a large mine, twice a small one's
strategos:building/iron_mine_large.TerritoryInfluence/weight: A building's weight: below a centre's, above a quarry's (TERR-01)
strategos:building/iron_mine_large.TerritoryInfluence/radius: Twelve blocks, a low weight: as the quarry (TERR-01)
strategos:building/iron_mine_large.TerritoryInfluence/root: Not a root: its land is connected only through a centre's (TERR-01)

strategos:building/storehouse.Cost/resources/stone: Half a barracks' stone: stone's third buyer, so a quarry pays for itself early

strategos:building/farmstead.Health/max: A house's and a half: a farm building of mud and brick

strategos:building/farmstead.Cost/time: Thirty-five seconds, 2.5 blocks a second for its 88

strategos:template/unit_soldier.Promotion/thresholds: Two hundred, five hundred and a thousand experience for the three ranks: two, then five, then ten kills of a hundred-resource soldier (a point of experience is a resource of what a unit has destroyed), so a rank is earned over a fight and the last over a campaign, and a soldier that is not at the front stays a recruit; our own starting values, to be tuned against QA-16 (CMB-11)
strategos:template/unit_soldier.Promotion/ranks: Per rank, hit points and attack times 1.05, 1.10 and 1.15: each rank is about half an equipment tier (the iron weapons and chainmail technologies are each about a tenth), and since hit points and damage both rise an elite is about 1.15 x 1.15 = 1.32 times as strong, the worth of three equipment tiers and no more, so a veteran army tells without deciding the match alone (a first try at 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3, an elite near 1.69, stalled the Ford battle bots); the sets replace one another and never compound, so rank 3 is 1.15 and not 1.05 times 1.10 times 1.15 (spec 2.8); melee hack and pierce and ranged pierce stand for every soldier's weapon, a path a unit lacks being 0 times the factor; our own starting values, to be tuned against QA-16 (CMB-11)
